title: What One Daily Survival Number Does

scenes.tts: Near Cambridge, birds took dark peppered moths more often than pale ones. The moth has a pale form, called typica, and a dark form, called carbonaria. Michael Majerus released moths there over six years. Cook and colleagues analysed his records. A dark moth survived each day at about zero point nine one times the rate of a pale one. What does that single number do to a wood full of moths?

scenes.tts: Try an exercise with invented numbers. A wood holds one thousand pale moths and one thousand dark moths. Say pale moths survive each day at zero point eight zero. Assume no migration, no reproduction and no change in rates.
scenes.caption: Try an exercise with invented numbers. A wood holds 1,000 pale moths and 1,000 dark moths. Say pale moths survive each day at 0.80. Assume no migration, no reproduction and no change in rates.
scenes.visual: two equal bars of 1,000; pale survival 0.80 chip; assumptions list
scenes.narration: Try an exercise with invented numbers. A wood holds 1,000 pale moths and 1,000 dark moths. Say pale moths survive each day at 0.80. Assume no migration, no reproduction and no change in rates.

scenes.tts: Dark moths survive at zero point nine zero nine times the pale rate. So dark daily survival is zero point eight zero times zero point nine zero nine. That is zero point seven two seven two. After one day, eight hundred pale moths are expected, and seven hundred twenty seven point two dark. That last figure is an expected count. A fraction of a moth is an expectation, not a moth.
scenes.caption: Dark moths survive at 0.909 times the pale rate. So dark daily survival is 0.80 times 0.909. That is 0.7272. After one day, 800 pale moths are expected, and 727.2 dark. That last figure is an expected count. A fraction of a moth is an expectation, not a moth.
scenes.visual: bars shrink to 800 and 727.2 as the arithmetic is written
scenes.narration: Dark moths survive at 0.909 times the pale rate. So dark daily survival is 0.80 times 0.909. That is 0.7272. After one day, 800 pale moths are expected, and 727.2 dark. That last figure is an expected count. A fraction of a moth is an expectation, not a moth.

scenes.tts: Now ask for the dark share among the survivors. Seven hundred twenty seven point two, out of one thousand five hundred twenty seven point two, is zero point four seven six. The dark share falls from fifty percent to forty seven point six percent. The pale rate and the starting thousands cancel. Only the ratio matters.
scenes.caption: Now ask for the dark share among the survivors. 727.2 out of 1,527.2 is 0.476. The dark share falls from 50% to 47.6%. The pale rate and the starting thousands cancel. Only the ratio matters.

scenes.narration: Now ask for the dark share among the survivors. 727.2 out of 1,527.2 is 0.476. The dark share falls from 50% to 47.6%. The pale rate and the starting thousands cancel. Only the ratio matters.

scenes.tts: The ratio compounds from day to day. Each extra day multiplies the dark to pale ratio by zero point nine zero nine again. After five days that ratio is zero point six two one. The dark share is then about thirty eight percent.
scenes.caption: The ratio compounds from day to day. Each extra day multiplies the dark to pale ratio by 0.909 again. After five days that ratio is 0.621. The dark share is then about 38%.

scenes.tts: Keep the limits. The zero point zero nine one is relative and per day, at one site over those years. It is not an annual decline, not an absolute death rate, and not a figure for all of Britain. Majerus's moths also disappeared, and only about twenty six percent of disappearances were witnessed bird attacks. A change in morph share is not yet a change in allele frequency. A relative daily survival compounds into a change in morph share, at one site.
